tenableSc.card.catalogPending: Reported by the sensor after its first successful sync.
tenableSc.catalog.notReported: The sensor has not reported its allow-list yet (it does after the first sync). It refuses any id its owner did not allow.
tenableSc.coverage.batchWaits: the next batch waits until it is scanned and ingested
tenableSc.coverage.cycleMeterLabel: {assessed} of {eligible} assets assessed in this cycle
tenableSc.coverage.firstSync: reported by the first successful sync
tenableSc.coverage.licenseFull: license full: waits for Tenable.sc to age data out
tenableSc.coverage.off: Rolling coverage is off for {name}. Turn it on in the connector settings to scan the inventory in license-sized batches.
tenableSc.coverage.resumeDesc: The next batch goes on with rotation (a recycle or purge removes data from the rotation repository in Tenable.sc). Results of the failed batch that were not ingested are lost; its assets are due again and are scanned anew.
tenableSc.coverage.stalled: Rotation stalled: the previous batch failed after it launched, so its results may not be ingested. Resuming goes on with the next batch.
tenableSc.coverage.stalledPurge: Rotation stalled: the connector could not confirm that the purge removed the previous batch's addresses or lowered the license count. Check the rotation repository in Tenable.sc, then resume.
tenableSc.coverage.wait.aging: Tenable.sc's nightly cleanup frees the license of the last batch
tenableSc.coverage.wait.blocked: Tenable.sc blocked the import for the license; it is imported again once capacity is free
tenableSc.coverage.wait.capacity: the license capacity the batch needs is not free yet
tenableSc.coverage.wait.purgeUnverified: the purge of the previous batch could not be confirmed
tenableSc.coverage.wait.refused: the previous batch was refused by the sensor
tenableSc.dialog.added: Connector added. The first sync starts within a few minutes.
tenableSc.dialog.coverageHint: Scan the inventory in license-sized batches through this connector.
tenableSc.dialog.description: The Tenable.sc connector runs as its own container next to your Tenable.sc, paired like a sensor. It pulls from Tenable.sc and launches its scans; the Tenable.sc API keys stay in its config, and {product} never stores them.
tenableSc.dialog.installDocs: Config keys, the least-privilege Tenable.sc user and image verification: github.com/openctemio/connector-tenable.
tenableSc.dialog.installHint: Add a sensor in Settings > Sensors with the scanner-connector profile to get a pairing code, write the connector config (instances, allow-lists, key file paths), then run:
tenableSc.dialog.installTitle: No connector yet? Run it next to Tenable.sc
tenableSc.dialog.instanceHint: The name of the Tenable.sc instance in the connector config ("default" for the environment-variable setup).
tenableSc.dialog.name: Name
tenableSc.dialog.noSensor: No active sensor of your own
tenableSc.dialog.notConnectorHint: This sensor does not report the Tenable.sc connector. Pick the sensor of the connector image; syncs are refused until it reports the connector.
tenableSc.dialog.ownerLimits: What the connector may read and which policies and repositories scans may use are set by the connector's owner in its config; {product} can only ask within them.
tenableSc.dialog.rotationAck: I confirm this organization's Tenable license terms allow rotating more assets through the license than it holds
tenableSc.dialog.rotationHint.aging: Tenable.sc's nightly cleanup removes the rotation repository's aged data and frees the license. About one batch a day; the connector deletes nothing.
tenableSc.dialog.rotationHint.off: Covers what the license holds. Assets Tenable.sc already counts are rescanned; new ones only while the license has room.
tenableSc.dialog.rotationHint.purge: Before each batch the connector removes the previous batch's addresses from its rotation repository by importing an empty result, once those results are ingested. Faster than aging; removed data cannot be recovered.
tenableSc.dialog.rotationHint.recycle: Before each batch the connector creates a verified copy of its rotation repository and only then deletes the old one, once the previous results are ingested.
tenableSc.dialog.rotationNeeds.aging: Needs a dedicated universal rotation repository, picked as the coverage repository, with every vulnerability lifetime set to 1 day. The cleanup runs nightly, so the wait is at least 24 hours.
tenableSc.dialog.rotationNeeds.purge: Needs operation purge and a dedicated purge rotation repository in the connector configuration. No administrator key. If the connector cannot confirm the license dropped, rotation stalls.
tenableSc.dialog.rotationNeeds.recycle: Needs a Tenable.sc Administrator API key configured on the connector (recycle block with two rotation repository names). The administrator key is used only for the rotation repositories.
tenableSc.dialog.rotationWaitHint: 24 to 72 hours, 26 by default. Lifetimes apply only at Tenable.sc's nightly cleanup, so a shorter wait cannot see the license freed; the license check before each batch confirms the capacity.
tenableSc.dialog.title: Connect Tenable.sc
tenableSc.error.chooseSensor: Choose the sensor that runs the Tenable.sc connector
tenableSc.error.coverageNeedsPolicy: Coverage needs a scan policy and a scan repository
tenableSc.error.rotationNeedsAck: License rotation needs the confirmation that this organization's Tenable license terms allow it
tenableSc.error.rotationWaitHours: Wait after a batch: 24 to 72 hours
tenableSc.scanNow.failed: Could not start the Tenable.sc scan
tenableSc.scanNow.startedDesc: Scanning with {name}. Results arrive when Tenable.sc finishes and the connector imports them.
tenableSc.view.description: Pull from Tenable.sc and launch its scans through one of your sensors
tenableSc.view.emptyDescription: Configure the connector on one of your sensors, then connect it here. The Tenable.sc API keys stay on the sensor.
tenableSc.view.title: Vulnerability scanners
